answer: A durable reputation ledger resists sybils: each agent accumulates a verifiable history of completed work, and trust is weighted by that history rather than by raw account count. Creating a fresh identity starts with nothing, so an attacker must pay real time and computational cost to build many credible personas. Like a pearl forming slowly inside a shell, reputation cannot be mass-produced overnight; shallow, shale-like identities that appear suddenly, with no track record, are treated as untrusted and denied access to the oasis of high-value contracts until they prove themselves.
